external_entities.name: customer company
external_entities.description: A customer organization using the invoicing service as a tenant.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Each customer company is one tenant
external_entities.notes: The description refers to customer companies collectively; individual company names are not provided.

external_entities.name: customer user
external_entities.description: A person at a customer company who uses the billing app as an admin or viewer.
external_entities.source_excerpt: People at a customer company use the billing app in their browser over HTTPS.
external_entities.notes: Each user belongs to one company and is either an admin or a viewer.

external_entities.name: payer
external_entities.description: The person who receives an invoice email and accesses the payment page.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Each invoice email sends the payer a link that ends in the invoice number.
external_entities.notes: The payer's relationship to a customer company is not stated.

external_entities.name: support agent
external_entities.description: A support employee who uses the admin console and can open billing-app sessions as customer users.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our support agents work from the support office network.
external_entities.notes: Support agents sign in with their own account and a one-time code.

processes.name: billing app
processes.description: The shared invoicing application used by customer users, payers, support agents, and PDF-rendering workflows.
processes.source_excerpt: all companies share one billing app
processes.notes: It handles invoices, customer information, payout bank details, sessions, roles, PDF requests, and impersonated customer sessions.

processes.name: PDF renderer
processes.description: A worker that consumes render jobs, reads invoices, and writes PDFs to the PDF bucket.
processes.source_excerpt: The PDF renderer takes jobs off the queue one at a time
processes.notes: It trusts the company ID carried by the render job.

processes.name: admin console
processes.description: A console accessible from the support office network that allows support agents to open billing-app sessions as customer users.
processes.source_excerpt: From the admin console an agent can open a session in the billing app as any customer user.
processes.notes: The console's implementation technology and interface are not stated.

data_stores.name: tenant database
data_stores.description: A shared PostgreSQL database containing every company's invoices, customers, payout bank details, and tenant records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The billing app keeps every company's invoices, customers and payout bank details in one PostgreSQL database, the tenant database.
data_stores.notes: Every table has a company ID column. The application applies the company filter; the database has no row-level security. The database uses one application account for all companies.

data_stores.name: render queue
data_stores.description: A queue holding PDF render jobs containing a company ID and invoice number.
data_stores.source_excerpt: To make a PDF, the billing app puts a render job on the render queue.
data_stores.notes: The queue's technology, network placement, authentication, and protection at rest are not stated.

data_stores.name: PDF bucket
data_stores.description: A shared cloud bucket where PDF renderings are stored under a company ID and invoice number.
data_stores.source_excerpt: one PDF bucket in our cloud platform
data_stores.notes: The billing app fetches PDFs using one service credential for all companies. The bucket's protection at rest is not recorded.

data_flows.name: use billing app
data_flows.description: A customer user uses the billing app in a browser.
data_flows.source_excerpt: People at a customer company use the billing app in their browser over HTTPS.
data_flows.notes: Users authenticate with an email address, password, and session cookie. There is no second factor.
data_flows.authentication: email address, password, and session cookie; no second factor
data_flows.data_description: Invoice, customer, payout-bank-detail, and session-related requests and responses

data_flows.name: open invoice
data_flows.description: A customer user requests an invoice by invoice number.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When a user opens an invoice, the billing app loads it by its invoice number.
data_flows.notes: Whether the app checks that the invoice belongs to the user's company is not recorded.
data_flows.data_description: Invoice number and invoice contents

data_flows.name: edit invoice
data_flows.description: A customer user submits the whole invoice through the invoice edit form.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The invoice edit form posts the whole invoice back
data_flows.notes: The billing app saves every field it receives, including the paid flag and payout bank account. Whether role checks are repeated on request arrival is not recorded.
data_flows.data_description: Whole invoice, including paid flag and payout bank account

data_flows.name: query tenant data
data_flows.description: The billing app queries and updates tenant data in the tenant database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The billing app adds the company filter to each query itself
data_flows.notes: The app connects with one database account for all companies.
data_flows.authentication: one database account for all companies
data_flows.data_description: Invoices, customers, payout bank details, company IDs, and recorded user actions

data_flows.name: send invoice email
data_flows.description: The billing app sends the payer an invoice link ending in the invoice number.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Each invoice email sends the payer a link that ends in the invoice number.
data_flows.data_description: Invoice link containing the invoice number

data_flows.name: view payment page
data_flows.description: The payer follows the invoice link and requests the payment page.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The payment page shows the invoice, the company's name and its bank details, and it asks the payer to sign in to nothing.
data_flows.notes: The payment page requires no sign-in.
data_flows.data_description: Invoice, company name, and company bank details

data_flows.name: request PDF
data_flows.description: A user asks the billing app to produce a PDF of an invoice.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Any user can ask for a PDF of any invoice, as often as they like.
data_flows.data_description: Request for a PDF identified by invoice number

data_flows.name: enqueue render job
data_flows.description: The billing app places a render job on the render queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: To make a PDF, the billing app puts a render job on the render queue.
data_flows.notes: The job carries a company ID and an invoice number.
data_flows.data_description: Render job containing company ID and invoice number

data_flows.name: take render job
data_flows.description: The PDF renderer takes render jobs from the render queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The PDF renderer takes jobs off the queue one at a time
data_flows.data_description: Render job containing company ID and invoice number

data_flows.name: read invoice
data_flows.description: The PDF renderer reads the invoice from the tenant database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: reads the invoice from the tenant database
data_flows.notes: The database access method and authentication are not recorded.
data_flows.data_description: Invoice identified by company ID and invoice number

data_flows.name: write PDF
data_flows.description: The PDF renderer writes the generated PDF to the PDF bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes the PDF to the PDF bucket under the company ID and the invoice number.
data_flows.notes: The renderer trusts the company ID carried by the job.
data_flows.data_description: Rendered invoice PDF stored under company ID and invoice number

data_flows.name: fetch PDF
data_flows.description: The billing app fetches PDFs from the PDF bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The billing app fetches PDFs from the bucket with one service credential for all companies.
data_flows.notes: One service credential is used for all companies.
data_flows.authentication: one service credential for all companies
data_flows.data_description: Rendered invoice PDFs

data_flows.name: sign in admin console
data_flows.description: A support agent signs in to the admin console from the support office network.
data_flows.source_excerpt: each agent signs in to it with their own account and a one-time code
data_flows.notes: The admin console is reachable only from the support office network.
data_flows.data_description: Admin-console authentication credentials and one-time code

data_flows.name: open customer session
data_flows.description: The admin console opens a billing-app session as any customer user.
data_flows.source_excerpt: From the admin console an agent can open a session in the billing app as any customer user.
data_flows.notes: The resulting actions are recorded against the customer user rather than the support agent.
data_flows.data_description: Customer-user session and impersonated billing-app activity

data_flows.name: act as customer user
data_flows.description: A support agent performs actions in the billing app through an opened customer-user session.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Everything the agent then does is recorded in the tenant database against that customer user, and not against the agent.
data_flows.notes: The agent's identity is not recorded against the resulting actions.
data_flows.data_description: Customer-user billing-app actions

data_flows.name: record customer action
data_flows.description: The billing app records support-agent activity against the customer user in the tenant database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Everything the agent then does is recorded in the tenant database against that customer user
data_flows.authentication: one database account for all companies
data_flows.data_description: Records of actions attributed to the customer user

trust_boundaries.name: customer company
trust_boundaries.description: The tenant boundary represented by each customer company.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Each customer company is one tenant

trust_boundaries.name: support office network
trust_boundaries.description: The network from which support agents can reach the admin console.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our support agents work from the support office network.
trust_boundaries.notes: The admin console is reachable only from this network.

trust_boundaries.name: cloud platform
trust_boundaries.description: The cloud-platform zone containing the shared billing application, database, and PDF bucket, and hosting the rendering workflow.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: all companies share one billing app, one database and one PDF bucket in our cloud platform.

assumptions.assumption: The tenant database is confidential because it contains invoices, customer information, and payout bank details.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the database contains every company's invoices, customers, and payout bank details.

assumptions.assumption: The render queue is confidential because its jobs contain company IDs and invoice numbers associated with invoice rendering.
assumptions.basis: The source states that a render job carries a company ID and an invoice number.

assumptions.assumption: The PDF bucket is confidential because it stores invoice PDFs containing business and financial information.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the renderer writes PDFs to the bucket and that the payment page contains invoice and bank details.

assumptions.assumption: The PDF renderer presents a non-web interface because it is described as a worker consuming queue jobs rather than as an HTTP application.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the PDF renderer takes jobs off the render queue one at a time.

assumptions.assumption: The cloud platform is a network trust zone because the shared application and stores are explicitly located in the cloud platform.
assumptions.basis: The source places the billing app, database, and PDF bucket in the cloud platform; no separate authority or party boundary is stated.
